<<The Physics of Road Damage>>
Road damage is not linearly proportional to axle weight but increases exponentially, often following the fourth-power law. This means that doubling the weight on an axle can result in sixteen times the stress on the pavement structure. Consequently, heavier vehicles cause significantly deeper cracking, rutting, and structural failure much faster than lighter ones. This principle is why transportation agencies strictly regulate maximum axle loads to extend infrastructure lifespan.
